title: Phase 4 — PATH-discovered subcommand dispatch
description: So the factory can own 'tk factory ...' from outside the binary. tk commands self-register via init() + rootCmd.AddCommand with no central registry, so removing a command file removes the command with zero edits elsewhere — the CLI surface cuts cleanly. What is missing is the other half: git-style dispatch where an unrecognised 'tk foo' resolves to a tk-foo binary on PATH. Chosen over a separate tkf binary (breaks every doc and all muscle memory) and over the factory shipping a superset tk (two binaries claiming one name is worse than either). The repo already has plugin/extension precedent in plugins/herdr-ticks and extensions/ticks-runner. Useful independently of the extraction.
acceptance_criteria: An external tk-hello binary on PATH is invocable as 'tk hello' with arguments and exit codes passed through faithfully. tk factory still resolves to the in-repo implementation. Unknown-command error messages still name real suggestions and do not degrade.
closed_reason:
CANCELLED 2026-08-27 on Peter's steer: "don't like the shape of that. let's not overload tk. I want to lean towards the unix philosophy, composable tools with minimum dependencies."

This epic was going to add git-style PATH dispatch to tk, so that an unrecognised 'tk foo' resolved to a tk-foo binary and ticfac could keep owning 'tk factory ...' from outside the binary. It is deleted from the plan, not deferred.

WHY IT WAS WRONG, on both halves of its own reasoning:

1. THE COST I CITED FOR A SEPARATE BINARY WAS NEAR-ZERO AND I OVERSTATED IT. The argument against 'ticfac deploy' was that it "breaks every doc and all muscle memory". Checked against every published tag including v0.31.1: ZERO cmd/tk/cmd/factory* files in any release. tk factory has never shipped. There are no users to break and no installed documentation to invalidate — the habit exists in one working tree.

2. DISPATCH WOULD MAKE TICKS BIGGER IN ORDER TO MAKE IT SMALLER. A PATH resolver, argument and exit-code passthrough, and a suggestion path that still behaves for genuinely unknown commands — all new code in tk, existing solely to serve a product that had just been removed from the repo for being out of scope. Meanwhile the mechanism actually required already exists: init() self-registration with no central registry means deleting a command file removes the command with zero edits elsewhere.

WHAT REPLACES IT: nothing. ticfac is its own binary — ticfac deploy, ticfac run, ticfac status. tk never learns that a factory exists. The composition happens where Unix puts it: two independent programs, one text interface. ticfac runs 'tk ... --json' to read the tracker; tk runs nothing. The dependency points one way.

CONSEQUENCES NOW OWNED BY PHASE 5 (5hm), noted there: the sandbox image installs two binaries rather than one plus a shim, and required-tk-commands splits into two lists each owned by the product that ships it. 'tk cloud ...' becomes 'ticfac ...'; whether 'cloud' survives as a SUBSTRATE NAME in .tick/runners.toml stays a Phase 6 question, and probably yes, since runners.toml already names herdr without ticks owning it.
